title: quick accent inserts `」` as `「` in the wechat desktop app

status.label: Likely Quick Accent mapping bug
status.detail: The symptom is specific and plausible as a character-selection bug in the Quick Accent insertion path.

next_action.label: Approve targeted Quick Accent fix design
next_action.reason: The report is precise and points to a likely character-selection regression in the insertion logic.

judgment.rationale: The report identifies a precise regression: the selected accent character is inserted as the mirrored glyph in a specific app, which fits an insertion-layer mapping bug rather than a general Quick Accent configuration failure.
evidence: The issue states typing `」` in WeChat causes `「` to be inserted instead.
The report is specific to Quick Accent and the observed mismatch is directional and app-specific.
The issue includes a diagnostic ZIP, which is enough for a focused boundary check on insertion mapping.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a targeted design to verify the Quick Accent selection/insertion mapping in the app-input path and add a regression test for mirrored character pairs.

fix_assessment.rationale: A fix is plausible but not yet grounded in the exact mapping/insertion boundary; the issue needs a focused design and validation on the fast-path selection logic.

proposed_fixes.title: Validate Quick Accent selected-character mapping before insertion
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The selected accent target may be mapped or normalized incorrectly before the text is injected, causing the mirrored glyph to be written for a specific input context.
plan: Inspect the Quick Accent selection and insertion pipeline for the active character mapping step.
Verify whether the selected glyph is transformed before being sent to the app or composed into the input stream.
Add a regression for mirrored punctuation pairs and verify the same character is inserted in WeChat Desktop.
verification: Repeat the exact `」`/`「` flow in WeChat Desktop and confirm the selected symbol is emitted without mirroring.
Add a unit/regression test covering the mapping pair to prevent future reversal.

confidence.rationale: The symptom is specific and consistent with a mapping bug, but the exact insertion boundary should be confirmed before patching.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent appears to insert the mirrored punctuation character in WeChat Desktop, suggesting a selection or injection-path mapping error rather than a general keyboard/layout problem.
known_information: The report is on PowerToys 0.100.2 via auto-update.
The issue is limited to a single character pair and a single desktop app.
The reporter included a PowerToys diagnostic ZIP.
The issue is labeled Issue-Bug and Needs-Triage only.
inferences: The problem is likely in the Quick Accent text insertion or normalization layer, not a broad app input issue.
issue_context.analysis: This is a credible fix candidate with a narrow boundary and enough specificity to justify a focused design review, but we still need one app-level validation and a small mapping check before patching.
initial_investigation: Read the public issue body and diagnostic attachment context.
Checked the issue label state and timeline; no maintainer position is present yet.
Inspected the likely Quick Accent insertion path only as necessary to confirm the report is within the known character-selection boundary.

information_gaps.information: Exact keyboard layout / app input method state during reproduction
information_gaps.why_needed: A layout or IME setting could cause the mirrored insert even when the internal mapping is correct.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the active keyboard layout, whether the app uses IME composition, and whether the same input is mirrored in another app.

actions.label: Approve Quick Accent mapping fix design

comment.body: Thanks for the precise reproduction. Please confirm whether the same mirrored insert happens in another app with the same keyboard layout and whether WeChat is using IME composition for the character. This helps distinguish a general Quick Accent mapping issue from an app-specific input path problem before we approve the design.
